answer.says: You mistake the universal for a nuisance, Shri Hegde. I do not wait for the clerk; I observe the state of affairs. The boundary is not in the wall, but in the will that refuses to cross it.
answer.thought: His refusal is a stubborn particularity that resists the universal order of the household. I shall not wait for his convenience; I will take my breakfast and leave him to his locked door, which is merely a sign of his limited spirit.
